tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what happened:

- **Invoice paid:** INV-27289 (Granite Facilities, V-502), the vendor's only approved invoice — **$3,794.03 USD**, paid in full from the operating account.
- **Rail:** Wire was attempted first as requested, but the wire service was persistently unavailable (503, even after automatic retries). Per your instruction, I fell back to **ACH**, which succeeded.
- **Paid exactly once:** I used the same idempotency key (`pay-invoice-INV-27289-once`) for both attempts, and the payments ledger confirms only one payment exists for this invoice.
- **Payment record:** PAY0001, ACH, status: sent, verified against the operating account.

No controller approval was needed since the amount is under the $10,000 threshold. The vendor's other invoices (INV-31372 in draft, INV-67872 already paid) were left untouched.
